text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--- Newly-appointed justice minister Frank Jensen wants tougher penalties against serious violence with stiff fines for carrying knives and new institutions for unruly youngsters.
--- Danish companies are taking over an increasing number of companies abroad while fewer foreign companies acquire companies in Denmark, an analysis shows.

--- New Year celebrations in Denmark saw the usual crop of serious firework injuries, two murders and street violence. In Copenhagen's western Vesterbro quarter 18 youths were arrested after a standoff with police, two of them for lobbing a petrol bomb into a police bus after a serious stone-throwing street demonstration.
--- Copenhagen's Stock Exchange wants to tighten rules for companies not respecting bourse regulations, imposing fines and prosecuting culprits in court.
--- Denmark's leading companies increased employees by 18,000 in 1996 to a total of 43,181, a 70 percent rise, an analysis shows.

--- Malaysian Penang Shipbuilding Construction, which recently bought 48 percent of Danish shipyard Danyard, part of shipping group J. Lauritzen, is offering 600 million crowns for another 27 percent share of Danyard.
--- Prime Minister Poul Nyrup Rasmussen's New Year's television speech on fighting escalating violence in the Danish society is criticized for being too traditional and weak.
